Name: Organizational Context
Evidence and rationale: ERP, payroll and customer database dependencies are documented in the PASTA threat model and vulnerability assessment scope. Regulatory obligations are not listed in one place.
Recommended action: Document legal, regulatory and contractual obligations and map them to systems.

Name: Risk Management Strategy
Evidence and rationale: A scored risk register with rating bands exists (risk-register-excel). No approved risk appetite statement or formal risk acceptance process.
Recommended action: Approve a risk appetite statement and a risk acceptance procedure with sign-off levels.

Name: Roles, Responsibilities, Authorities
Evidence and rationale: Risk owners are named in the register. No documented cybersecurity roles or responsibility matrix beyond risk ownership.
Recommended action: Publish a RACI for security, risk and compliance activities.

Name: Policy
Evidence and rationale: The employee guide cites three policies (report phishing, no credentials by link, IT never asks for passwords). No full policy set with annual review.
Recommended action: Create and approve access control, change management, incident response and acceptable use policies; review annually.

Name: Oversight
Evidence and rationale: Risk summaries can be produced, but there is no scheduled report of risk posture to leadership.
Recommended action: Present the risk summary and top risks to leadership each quarter.

Name: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management
Evidence and rationale: Several critical vendors were not reassessed in over 18 months (risk R-15). Vendor tiering and review are defined in third-party-risk-assessment.
Recommended action: Adopt vendor tiering, a 12-month reassessment cycle and SOC 2 report review.

Name: Asset Management
Evidence and rationale: Core systems are known. A legacy file server with a shared admin account (R-12) was found outside normal administration, so the inventory is incomplete.
Recommended action: Build and reconcile an asset inventory with owner and data classification for every system.

Name: Risk Assessment
Evidence and rationale: NIST SP 800-30 style assessment, PASTA threat model, ITGC testing and a scored register exist. Assessments are one-time, not on a set cycle.
Recommended action: Run risk assessments on a fixed annual cycle and after major changes.

Name: Improvement
Evidence and rationale: Incident journal reflections and ITGC recommendations capture lessons. There is no tracker that follows each improvement to closure.
Recommended action: Track every audit and incident recommendation to closure in the risk register.

Name: Identity Management, Authentication, Access Control
Evidence and rationale: ITGC tests found terminated users still active (2 of 4), overdue reviews (2 of 14) and a segregation of duties conflict. VPN has no MFA (R-10) and a legacy server uses shared admin credentials (R-12).
Recommended action: Automate deprovisioning from HR, enforce MFA, remove shared admin accounts, and run semi-annual access reviews.

Name: Awareness & Training
Evidence and rationale: A plain-language phishing and malware guide exists. No phishing simulations or completion and click-rate metrics.
Recommended action: Run quarterly phishing simulations and report click and report rates.

Name: Data Security
Evidence and rationale: Payroll data sat in unencrypted spreadsheets (R-14), database connections use deprecated SSL (R-08), and the customer database was reachable from the internet (R-05).
Recommended action: Encrypt sensitive data, enforce TLS 1.2 or higher, restrict database access to an allow-list.

Name: Platform Security
Evidence and rationale: A critical ERP vulnerability is unpatched (R-09) and 4 of 8 production changes lacked independent approval (ITGC test, D-04).
Recommended action: Patch the ERP, block unapproved changes in the ticketing system, and set patch SLAs by severity.

Name: Technology Infrastructure Resilience
Evidence and rationale: A full restoration test of the financial database was completed (R-13 closed). Public exposure of the customer database remains an architecture gap.
Recommended action: Segment the database tier and repeat restoration tests every year.

Name: Continuous Monitoring
Evidence and rationale: A Python script detects brute force, off-hours and geographic anomalies in exported authentication logs. It is not continuous or alerting.
Recommended action: Centralize logs in a SIEM and schedule detections with alerts to an on-call owner.

Name: Adverse Event Analysis
Evidence and rationale: Indicator analysis (Pyramid of Pain, VirusTotal) and packet analysis comparisons show analysis skills. No written triage criteria across event types.
Recommended action: Define triage criteria and severity levels for alerts.

Name: Incident Management
Evidence and rationale: A phishing playbook exists. There is no tested ransomware runbook (R-11).
Recommended action: Write and tabletop-test a ransomware runbook; extend the playbook set to other incident types.

Name: Incident Analysis
Evidence and rationale: The incident handler's journal documents investigation steps and NIST lifecycle mapping. Evidence handling is not formalized.
Recommended action: Add an evidence handling and chain of custody procedure.

Name: Incident Response Reporting & Communication
Evidence and rationale: The phishing playbook includes escalation. There is no external communication or regulator notification plan.
Recommended action: Add a communication plan covering leadership, customers, regulators and law enforcement.

Name: Incident Mitigation
Evidence and rationale: Containment steps exist for phishing and malware (disconnect, do not self-remediate, call IT). Not tested for ransomware.
Recommended action: Test containment steps during the ransomware tabletop exercise.

Name: Incident Recovery Plan Execution
Evidence and rationale: Backup restoration has been tested once. No documented recovery plan with recovery time and recovery point objectives.
Recommended action: Document recovery time and recovery point objectives and a prioritized recovery plan for ERP and payroll.

Name: Incident Recovery Communication
Evidence and rationale: No recovery communication procedure is documented.
Recommended action: Add recovery status updates and a post-incident report template to the incident plan.
